conviction_note: The two measurements roughly agree: the findings sum to +0.4 and the scaled number is +0.48 (p_up 53, abs 8.0). On the evidence, the peers that printed this week (Azure 48% vs 44% expected, Google Cloud +103% vs 90% expected) point to AWS beating the 38% consensus. That is offset by how this week rewarded such beats: Alphabet fell 8-12% on capex, FCF and an EPS miss despite its Cloud beat, Microsoft gave back its after-hours gain, and Amazon is the hyperscaler with negative trailing FCF and a likely capex raise. The lean is therefore barely above 50. The baseline file failed (bars_failed), so the scale comes from the 6.6-7.4% option-implied move in press sources and recent reactions (+6.0, -9.7, +2.1, +15 to +20).
bar: Revenue consensus $202.10B (Investing.com, https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/amazon-stock-setup-into-todays-earnings-what-could-push-shares-higher-or-lower-93CH-4983838, 2026-10-29) or $202.25B (24/7 Wall St, https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/, 2026-10-29). Both sit at the top of the company's $197.0-202.0B guide (8-K ex99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm, 2026-07-30). EPS consensus is $1.96-1.97, with a range of $1.72-2.32, and is noisy because of non-operating Anthropic and OpenAI marks. Operating income consensus is about $26.2B against a $22.5-26.5B guide. AWS consensus is 37.8-38% YoY, about $45.6-45.7B (FactSet via CNBC; 24/7 Wall St; Yahoo 2026-10-27). Two or more sources agree on each, so the bar counts as sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 100-107M shares (~1% of float), with days to cover of 2.25 on 2026-06-15 (Benzinga, https://benzinga.com/quote/AMZN/short-interest) and 2.8 on 2026-07-15 (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/amzn/shortinterest). That is not crowded, and I found no October settlement. I found no 25-delta skew for this event; the baseline file failed (status bars_failed: HTTPError), so it carries no skew, spot or reaction history. The option-implied move is ~6.6% (Bloomberg data via Investing.com, 2026-10-22/29) or ~7.4% (Pepperstone, 2026-10-23). Into the print the stock fell from $262.37 (Oct 21) to $254.60 (Oct 28 close) and was ~$246 midday Oct 29 (-3%) on Alphabet's post-print slide. That is a ~6% drawdown in a week into the print, below the 52-week high of $287.20.

findings.finding: Two peers reported after Amazon last spoke (July 30), and both clouds beat and accelerated well above expectations. Microsoft Azure grew 48% vs 44% expected ($33.17B vs $32.32B), up from 43% the quarter before. Google Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B vs ~90% / $28.7B expected, with TPU systems sales a 'meaningful contributor'. AWS consensus is only 38% (~$45.7B), one point above Q2's 37%, while Jassy said capacity is sold out through 2026 and the backlog is $496B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When AWS last surprised (Q2 2026, 37% at its fastest in 18 quarters vs low-30s expected), AMZN rose +15.3% (Pepperstone) to +19.8% (Investing.com) the next day. In Q1 2026, with AWS at 28%, the reaction was +2.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: AWS consensus (FactSet 37.8%) implies roughly +1pt of acceleration. Azure accelerated +5pts and Google Cloud ~+20pts in the same quarter. If the street had marked AWS up to the peers, consensus would sit at 40%+ like BofA's, and AMZN would not have fallen 3% in sympathy with Alphabet the day after the peer prints. But AWS growth is capacity-bound rather than demand-bound, so peer demand transmits only as fast as AWS can add capacity. This is a proxy, which is why it is sized well below the Q2 reaction.
findings.independence: Alphabet's primary release confirms the Google Cloud figures: $30,709M vs $15,157M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm, 2026-10-28). The AWS backlog of $496B and the 2027 capacity 'lion's share reserved' come from the Amazon Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/amazon-amzn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Both are peer and proxy evidence, not AWS's own Q3 number.

findings.finding: Several sell-side models sit above the 38% AWS consensus going in: BofA (Justin Post) at 40% with a 39% AWS margin, and BNP Paribas at 43-45%. Wells Fargo expects Q4 operating income guidance near the high end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same AWS line as finding 1: +15 to +20% in Q2 2026 on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced: published broker notes are wire copy, and the buy-side whisper likely sits nearer 40% than 38%. That raises the bar a beat must clear for a positive reaction. Kept small for that reason.
findings.independence: Investing.com 2026-10-29 says the bull case needs ~35%+ growth (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/amazon-stock-setup-into-todays-earnings-what-could-push-shares-higher-or-lower-93CH-4983838). This is a different source from finding 1 but the same AWS line, and is not independent of the peer read-through.

findings.finding: This week's reaction function punished hyperscaler capex and FCF burn even on cloud beats. Alphabet fell ~8% after hours and ~12% midday Oct 29 to $286.17 despite Cloud +103%: Q3 FCF was -$9.07B, capex $51.4B, and EPS of $2.12 missed on an $8.7B equity-securities loss. Amazon is the most exposed to the same verdict: trailing FCF was -$7.6B at June 30, long-term debt was $128.9B (from $65.6B at year-end), the 2026 capex guide of $220B was already raised once for memory costs, and UBS sees spending above $300B by 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (Feb 5, 2026): revenue beat ($213.4B vs $211.3B) but the stock fell 9.7% when the $200B 2026 capex guide overshadowed results (Investing.com table; Morningstar headline). In Q2 2026 the capex raise to $220B came with AWS acceleration and the stock rose 15-20%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: AMZN fell ~3% today in sympathy, and capex/FCF is the most-discussed debate in every preview. The unpriced part is whether Amazon raises 2026 capex again or gives a 2027 number. A capex raise read through Alphabet's verdict would show as a further gap down, which today's -3% has not fully discounted given the 7%+ implied move.
findings.independence: Alphabet's primary release confirms Q3 FCF of $(9,065)M and capex of $51,355M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm). Amazon's own trailing FCF of -$7.6B is from its Q2 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm). Amazon's 2026 capex guide rose $200B to $220B on memory costs (https://www.fierce-network.com/cloud/memory-drives-amazon-capex-another-20b-2026).

findings.finding: The revenue bar sits at the top of the guide. Consensus of $202.1-202.25B equals the $202.0B top of the $197-202B guide, which carries ~400bp of Prime Day timing drag and ~80bp of FX drag. Amazon beat the top of its revenue guide in Q2 ($200.6B vs a $199B top). Consensus operating income of ~$26.2B sits near the $26.5B top.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Total-revenue beats have not decided the move: Q4 2025 revenue beat ~1% and the stock fell 9.7%; Q1 2026 beat 2.5% and it rose 2.1%; Q3 2025 beat 1.3% and it rose 6.0% (Investing.com table).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the street already models the top of the guide. Only a beat well above $202B (a repeat of Q2's 0.8% over the top) or a miss inside the range would be news. Sized near zero; this lands inside what the company guided.
findings.independence: Visible Alpha pre-Q consensus of $203.9B revenue and $25.4B operating income, versus the guide (S&P Global, https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/08/amazon-postq-aws-reaccelerates-as-ai-investment-pushes-capex-higher). Shares the guidance document with finding 9.

findings.finding: Peer commentary points to delayed third-party data-centre capacity in the quarter. Microsoft's capex of $45.2B came in under the $50.7B consensus, which it blamed on delayed third-party capacity pushing deliveries into the second half of its fiscal year. Alphabet's capex was also under consensus ($51.36B vs $55.09B). AWS revenue is capacity-gated (Jassy: not enough capacity for 2026 demand), so a similar delay would cap Q3 AWS upside even with demand intact. The offset is lower capex and better FCF.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not directly observed for AMZN; capacity commentary drove the Q2 2026 AWS reacceleration narrative (+15-20%).
findings.why_not_priced: No preview I found connects the peers' capex shortfalls to AWS revenue timing; previews treat AWS capacity as only growing. Sign is mixed (revenue cap vs FCF relief), so it is sized small and slightly negative.
findings.independence: Alphabet's capex of $51,355M is confirmed in its 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm). Shares the 24/7 Wall St article with finding 3, but this is a different fact (capex timing vs the FCF reaction).

findings.finding: Prime Big Deal Days (Oct 6-7, 2026), the first data point on Amazon's Q4 that the Q4 guide will be set against: Adobe measured US online spending of $9.86B, +8.5% YoY, slightly below Adobe's own $9.9B / +9.2% forecast.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 guidance and capex together drove the -9.7% in Feb 2026; I could not isolate a reaction to the event data itself.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three weeks and an industry-wide figure, not Amazon's own sales, so mostly priced. A slight miss against forecast is the only incremental content.
findings.independence: Forecast comparison from Chain Store Age (https://chainstoreage.com/adobe-prime-big-deal-days-spending-rise-9-99b). Same Adobe dataset.

findings.finding: The digital ad peer read is mixed against Amazon's ad consensus of $20.91B (+18% YoY). Meta's Q3 revenue grew 26.1% to $64.6B. Alphabet's total Google advertising grew only ~11% ($82.0B vs $74.2B), with YouTube ads +9% and Network +1%. Amazon ads grew 26% in Q2, helped by Prime Day falling in that quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ads have been a secondary line; Q2's +26% came alongside the AWS-driven +15-20%. No isolated reaction found.
findings.why_not_priced: An 18% consensus is an 8pt deceleration from Q2. Prime Day timing explains perhaps 3-5pts of that, so the bar looks modest next to Meta's +26%, but Google's +11% argues the market is not uniformly strong. Net small positive.
findings.independence: Meta's +26.1% from 24/7 Wall St (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/). Proxy only.

findings.finding: Non-operating marks will make GAAP EPS diverge from the $1.96 consensus (range $1.72-2.32). Q2 carried $53.4B of non-operating gains, mostly Anthropic, and $5.75 EPS. I found no new Anthropic priced round in Q3 (the last was the $965B Series H on 2026-05-28, inside Q2). Amazon funded about $21.3B more of OpenAI after June 30. Alphabet's $8.7B equity-securities loss this quarter cost it $0.55 of EPS and an 'EPS miss' headline that fed its sell-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The market looked through Q2's $5.75 vs $1.81 EPS and traded the AWS line instead. Alphabet's equity loss this week coincided with a 12% fall, but alongside a capex/FCF story.
findings.why_not_priced: Below operating income, with no path to the guide. The sign of any Q3 mark is unknown, since no Q3 priced round was found. Sized at zero; it can only distort the headline EPS print for an hour.
findings.independence: Q2 other income of $53.4B 'primarily from our investments in Anthropic' (Amazon 8-K ex99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm). The OpenAI tranche figure is from Pepperstone (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview).

findings.finding: About $1.2B of Q2 operating income was one-off: ~$600M of tariff refunds, which the CFO called 'the significant majority of refunds we expect', and a ~$551-600M energy-derivative fair-value gain booked mostly in AWS. Q3 guidance assumes no energy-derivative remeasurement. So Q2's 39.4% AWS margin is flattered, and the 39% AWS margin modelled by BofA assumes a repeat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AWS margin surprises have mattered for AMZN (Q2's 39.4% was part of the +15-20%), but the one-off component itself has no isolated reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus AWS margin near Q2's level may not strip out the energy gain. A sequential AWS margin dip could read as deterioration. Most of this is remeasurement noise, so sized as a fraction of operating-profit-equivalent dollars.
findings.independence: The Q3 guide's exclusion of energy-derivative remeasurement is in Amazon's 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm). Shares that document with finding 4.

findings.finding: Financing to fund the capex ramp: Amazon closed four sterling note series on 2026-09-14 (£1.25B 5.200% 2029 plus three £1B series), following USD ($36.9B, March), EUR (March), CAD (C$13.97B, June) and USD (July) offerings. Long-term debt was $128.9B at June 30. The money buys data-centre capacity against a $496B AWS backlog growing at triple digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction; debt growth feeds the FCF debate in finding 3.
findings.why_not_priced: Fully public 8-Ks. The funding is corroborated by the backlog and the sold-out capacity, so per the financing question the sign is zero rather than distress. Its market relevance runs through finding 3, so it is not counted again here.
findings.independence: Backlog of $496B from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/amazon-amzn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: In September 2026 a federal court approved expanded automatic redress payments under the FTC Prime settlement (users of 11-20 Prime benefits, up to $200 total, payments from Oct 1). More than $845M had been paid by September, from the $1.5B consumer fund accrued with the 2025 settlement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The original $2.5B FTC charge depressed Q3 2025 operating income (to $17.4B), which makes this quarter's year-on-year comparison easy. No reaction to the expansion found.
findings.why_not_priced: Likely paid from the existing accrued fund, so there is probably no new charge. If Amazon booked an incremental accrual it falls outside the guide (which excludes legal settlements). Sized at zero.

findings.finding: Company-level forward demand stated on the Q2 call: AWS backlog of $496B (up from ~$364B the quarter before) growing at triple digits YoY. Jassy said 'the lion's share' of planned 2027 AWS capacity is already reserved and that Amazon will not have enough capacity for 2026 demand. Anthropic committed over $100B over 10 years for up to 5GW on AWS, with nearly 1GW before end-2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog disclosure accompanied the Q2 +15-20% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; it has been public since July 30. The incremental piece is the Q3 backlog print: peers' backlogs (Google ~$514B at Q2) and Azure's acceleration suggest another large step, but that is inference.
findings.independence: Anthropic's own announcement of the AWS expansion (https://convergedigest.com/anthropic-secures-5-gw-of-ai-compute-in-expanded-100b-aws-deal/). Shares the call transcript with finding 9.

baseline_tension: The baseline is empty (bars_failed), so there is no sealed skew. Against the run-in (-6% from Oct 21 to today, -3% today in sympathy with Alphabet), the positive AWS read-through cuts against the price, while the capex/FCF finding agrees with it. Net, the evidence is close to balanced, which is why p_up is 53.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs at a fraction): the energy-derivative and tariff-refund finding went from -0.3 to -0.2, since it is remeasurement noise with no path to the guide.
Lesson 3 (resolve your own caveat): the peer capacity-delay finding argues both ways (revenue cap vs FCF relief) and went from -0.3 to -0.2.

Lessons 1 and 'what has worked' (peer print after the company last spoke): the AWS read-through stays at +1.5, because AMZN has paid for the AWS line (+15-20% in Q2). The reaction-function risk is carried by the separate capex/FCF finding at -1.5, not by shrinking this one again.
Lessons 6 and 7 left the rest standing: the bar is sourced from two or more agreeing sources, short interest is ~1% so not crowded, and no skew was available to argue against.
